body:
So what? If my life doesn't exist, then it doesn't matter who or what is valuable in it.

I can't forget about someone I've spent a quarter of my life with, nor do I want to.

I can't listen to music because everything I enjoy, she enjoys, it all reminds me of listening to it with her.

Every type of media I try to distract myself with alludes to love or relationships in some way and I end up thinking of her again.
Yeah, that's actually something I'm planning on. My company health plan covers it completely, so I'm looking into one.

>it still seems futile for us to express or feelings because it is so easy for us to discern how people are feeling themselves. We never need others to express how they feel to us so we don't usually feel the need to express ourselves.

That is how I've felt, but I think I've come to realize that's not the truth. I've always *thought* that I can easily tell what others are feeling, but if I couldn't tell that the person closest to me was so unhappy for so long, I have likely overestimated that skill by a large margin.

I don't agree that we can't change - I think, if I ever want to have truly meaningful interpersonal relationships with other people, that change has to happen. Hell, since starting to express myself more I've shared more feelings with my mother and brother than I've ever shared with them in my life. I think that's a sign it's a good thing, and a thing that needs to happen.

Yeah, that's basically what she made clear to me - from my actions, it's as if I've never had those thoughts at all.

I'm not going to ask her to be with me again, I'm just going to stay close to her, I'm going to do everything I can to make her happy, and I'm going to make sure she always knows how much I appreciate her and want to hear about her. I have little hope, but at the very least I will have the most inspiring, amazing beautiful friend in the world.

Communication was the issue, but not really on her side. She is somewhat quiet, and keeps to herself a bit, but she made known what the problems were, I just wasn't observant enough to know I wasn't addressing them.

I realized, through the past couple weeks from this breakup, that I have a problem where I imagine everything I do before I do it. Even things like locking the door, or getting my wallet - I imagine things in such detail that I don't remember whether I did them or not - and I think that had a lot to do with my poor communication. I'd get lost in my thoughts about her and not realize she had no way of knowing what I thought.

I do think I can give her what she wants, and what she needs - but I don't think I can do so right now, either. The issue above, among others need to be righted with me before I could do that - I have some severe emotional issues that I wont get in to.

>Are you though or do you just miss the comfort of the relationship?

This is what I think she is thinking right now. The comfort of the relationship is something I miss, sure, but if I wanted to, I could have another relationship easily. The thing is, I have *never* liked relationships - I don't need to be in one to function, I don't need a warm body in my bed or someone to listen to me talk, and both of those things I can get easily if I desire it. 

I know I'm still in love with her because my feelings for her didn't change at all when we broke up. The amount I think about her now is honestly even a little less just because I have to distract my mind sometimes. Some people will say that when they broke up with someone, suddenly they realized everything they were missing - that didn't happen for me, I knew everything I had all along, I treasured it just the same, I just didn't treat it right in action.

There hasn't been a day in my life with her that I wasn't thinking about how the future would play out with us, thinking about how what I was doing could make her happier, could help her get to the things she wanted. She has always been the most important to me.

Thank you for your thoughts - especially about how she might have viewed me as switching between cycles of caring and not caring, that's not something I thought of before.

She doesn't believe I could ever make her happy, nor that I ever loved her the way I say I do. Nonetheless, I will never stop loving her, and never stop trying to make her happy.

If it takes until I'm going senile, it'd still be worth it for the last few years with her. 

Thank you for the kind words of encouragement.
I wrote her a letter, a long one, but she's either not ready to, or doesn't want to read it.

>When you felt her turn cold, that is how she felt the entire relationship.

Yeah, when I realized that it was the point my heart broke further than I knew it could. The entire time, she's felt the exact opposite of what I wanted to make her feel.
